summary: 八岁即位，霍光辅政，盐铁之议、轻徭薄赋，与民休息；年二十一崩而无嗣。
summary_en: Ascending at eight with Huo Guang as regent, he brought the Salt and Iron Debate, light corvée and taxes, and rest for the people; he died at twenty-one without issue.

timeline.title: 钩弋子生

timeline.summary_en: The youngest son of Emperor Wu, by Lady Zhao, the Hook-Yi Lady; the exact year is unrecorded and back-calculated from his age at accession.

timeline.title: 立太子并即位
timeline.summary: 武帝疾病，立弗陵为太子，霍光受遗诏辅政；明日武帝崩，太子即皇帝位。
timeline.summary_en: With Emperor Wu ill, Fuling was made heir apparent and Huo Guang received the testamentary charge; the next day Wu died and the heir took the throne.

timeline.title: 益州廉头姑缯反
timeline.summary: 益州廉头、姑缯民反，遣吕破胡募吏民及发犍为、蜀郡兵击破之。
timeline.summary_en: The Lientou and Guzeng peoples of Yizhou revolted; Lü Poho was sent to levy men and troops from Qianwei and Shu commanderies and crushed them.

timeline.title: 盐铁会议
timeline.summary: 问郡国贤良文学民所疾苦，议罢盐铁酒榷均输，后罢榷酤。
timeline.summary_en: The worthy and literary men of the commanderies were asked about the people's grievances; the debate over the salt, iron, liquor monopoly, and equal transport led to abolition of the liquor monopoly.

timeline.title: 燕王旦上官桀谋反
timeline.title_en: Plot of the King of Yan and Shangguan Jie
timeline.summary: 燕王旦与上官桀、桑弘羊等谋杀霍光废帝，事败族诛，旦自杀。
timeline.summary_en: The king of Yan, Shangguan Jie, Sang Hongyang, and others plotted to kill Huo Guang and depose the emperor; the plot failed, the plotters were executed with their clans, and the king killed himself.

timeline.title: 霍光权固
timeline.summary: 诛反者后霍光专制朝事，昭帝「委任霍光」。
timeline.summary_en: After the purge Huo Guang dominated the court, the emperor entrusting everything to him.

timeline.title: 傅介子斩楼兰王
timeline.title_en: Fu Jiezi Slays the King of Loulan
timeline.summary: 平乐监傅介子使西域，计斩楼兰王安归，更名其国为鄯善。
timeline.summary_en: Fu Jiezi, superintendent of Pingle, went to the Western Regions, slew the Loulan king Angui by stratagem, and renamed the state Shanshan.

timeline.title: 昭帝崩
timeline.summary: 崩，年二十一，无嗣；大将军霍光等议所立。
timeline.summary_en: He died at twenty-one without issue; General-in-Chief Huo Guang and the others deliberated on a successor.

timeline.title: 立昌邑王贺
timeline.summary_en: Prince He of Changyi was summoned and enthroned.

timeline.title: 废昌邑王
timeline.summary: 贺即位二十七日，行淫乱，霍光与群臣奏皇太后废之。
timeline.summary_en: Twenty-seven days into his reign He behaved dissolutely; Huo Guang and the ministers petitioned the empress dowager to depose him.

timeline.title: 迎立宣帝
timeline.title_en: Emperor Xuan Called to the Throne
timeline.summary: 光等奏立武帝曾孙病已，是为孝宣皇帝。
timeline.summary_en: Huo Guang and the others memorialized to raise Emperor Wu's great-grandson Bingyi, the Emperor Xuan.

bio_md:
# 汉昭帝 · 主要事迹

刘弗陵是[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]少子，母钩弋夫人。后元二年，武帝疾病，立八岁的弗陵为太子，以大司马大将军霍光受遗诏辅政；武帝既崩，太子即位。一个八岁的皇帝面对的是武帝末年虚耗的海内、猜忌的宗室和虎视眈眈的辅臣——而昭帝朝竟在霍光的执掌下平稳度过十三年，史称「知时务之要」。

昭帝朝的政策主线是休养生息：始元六年二月，诏郡国举贤良文学问民疾苦，围绕盐铁酒榷均输展开辩论，即盐铁会议，会后罢榷酤；轻徭薄赋，与民休息，接续文景遗风。边防方面，元凤四年傅介子使西域，计斩楼兰王安归，更名其国为鄯善，西域方向保持了汉家的声威。

朝局并不平静。始元年间燕王旦勾结上官桀、桑弘羊等，谋诛霍光废帝；昭帝亲察其诈，事败，诸人族诛，霍光遂专制朝事。关于昭帝本人，史载他早慧而明于判狱，但十四岁后权力实际尽归霍光，他在位后期的形象，更多是辅政制度的背景板。

元平元年四月，昭帝崩，年二十一，无嗣。霍光先迎立[[han-changyi|昌邑王贺]]，贺在位二十七日以行淫乱被废，复立武帝曾孙[[han-xuan-di|汉宣帝]]。昭帝一朝所积累的休养政策与辅政结构，延续为昭宣之治，成为西汉中叶最后的安定时代。

> 参考：点校本《汉书》卷007《昭帝纪》、卷008《宣帝纪》，《霍光传》、《傅介子传》、《武五子传》，《盐铁论》，谭图第 2 册。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Fuling was the youngest son of

, by the Hook-Yi Lady. In the second year of the Later era, with Emperor Wu ill, the eight-year-old Fuling was made heir apparent, and General-in-Chief Huo Guang received the testamentary charge as regent; when Wu died, the heir took the throne. An eight-year-old emperor faced the realm drained by the late campaigns of Wu's reign, a jealous royal house, and watchful regents — and yet the Zhao reign passed thirteen years in stability under Huo Guang's hand. The historians said he "knew the essentials of the times."

The policy line of his reign was rest and recuperation: in the second month of the sixth Shiyuan year he ordered the commanderies to recommend worthy and literary men and asked them about the people's grievances, opening the debate over the salt, iron, and liquor monopolies and the equal-transport system — the Salt and Iron Debate — after which the liquor monopoly was abolished. Corvée and taxes were lightened and the people rested, in the spirit of the Wen-Jing age. On the frontier, in the fourth Yuanfeng year, Fu Jiezi went to the Western Regions, slew the Loulan king Angui by stratagem, and renamed the state Shanshan, preserving the prestige of Han in that direction.

The court was not quiet. In the Shiyuan years the king of Yan plotted with Shangguan Jie, Sang Hongyang, and others to kill Huo Guang and depose the emperor; Zhao himself detected the forgery of the plot's letter. The affair failed, the plotters were executed with their clans, and Huo Guang came to dominate the court absolutely. The histories credit Zhao with early wisdom and a clear eye in judging cases, yet after the age of fourteen real power belonged entirely to Huo Guang; in his later years the emperor's figure recedes into the background of the regency.

In the fourth month of the first Yuanping year Emperor Zhao died at twenty-one, without issue. Huo Guang first summoned
; He was deposed after twenty-seven dissolute days, and Emperor Wu's great-grandson

was raised to the throne. The recuperative policies and regency structure accumulated in the Zhao reign continued as the Zhao-Xuan recovery, the last tranquil age of the Western Han's middle period.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 7 (Benji of Emperor Zhao) and ch. 8 (Benji of Emperor Xuan); the biographies of Huo Guang, Fu Jiezi, and the Five Sons of Wu; the *Discourses on Salt and Iron*; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2.
